angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 563,517 km at 69.76 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.3348 +/- 0.0132 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01): 69.76 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.81 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Carleo et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1648 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549f1958C/abstract): 563,517 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.83 +/- 0.06 solar masses from Carleo et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1648 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549f1958C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4850 +/- 50 K from Carleo et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1648 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549f1958C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Carleo et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1648 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549f1958C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1648.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.540, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
